Spue
spū
v. (to vomit; rendering Greek emeo, Hebrew qi and qayah)
Old English spīwan. The Authorized Version keeps the plain word, and gives it to the land in Leviticus and to the Lord in Revelation.

Biblical Definition

To Laodicea: “So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth” (Rev 3:16). To Israel entering Canaan: “That the land spue not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spued out the nations that were before you” (Lev 18:28); “keep all my statutes… that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out” (Lev 20:22). To the nations, from the cup: “Drink ye, and be drunken, and spue, and fall, and rise no more” (Jer 25:27).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines spew as to vomit; to puke; to eject from the stomach; to eject, to cast forth.

expand to see more

SPEW, v.t. To vomit; to puke; to eject from the stomach.

2. To eject; to cast forth.

3. To cast out with abhorrence.

Key Scripture

Rev 3:16 — "So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth."

Lev 18:28 — "That the land spue not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spued out the nations that were before you."

Lev 20:22 — "Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out."

Jer 25:27 — "Therefore thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Drink ye, and be drunken, and spue, and fall, and rise no more, because of the sword which I will send among you."

Modern Corruption

The sentimental Christ cannot be sick of anything, and the Lord told a church He would spue it out of His mouth.

expand to see more

Revelation 3:16 is the least polite sentence the glorified Christ ever spoke, and He spoke it to a church. He did not say He would rebuke Laodicea, or discipline her, or remove her candlestick; He said He would vomit her, and the plainness is the point — a lukewarm church is not disappointing to Him but nauseating. The Christ of the modern pulpit has no stomach; He accepts, affirms, and accompanies, and is never once revolted. Leviticus 18 gives the older form of the same physiology: the land itself vomited out the Canaanites for their abominations, and Israel is warned that the land has no favourites — defile it, and it will spue you out as it spued them. Creation is not neutral toward abomination. It gags.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek emeo (G1692), to vomit; Hebrew qi (H6958) and qayah (H7006), to vomit, spue out.

expand to see more

Greek emeo (G1692) — to vomit, spue; Revelation 3:16 only.

Hebrew qi (H6958) — to vomit out; Leviticus 18:25, 18:28, 20:22, Jonah 2:10; qayah (H7006), Jeremiah 25:27.

Usage

"“I will spue thee out of my mouth” — a Christ who can be sick of a church."

"“That the land spue not you out also” — the land has no favourites."

"“Drink ye, and be drunken, and spue, and fall” — the cup of the nations."
